# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty import ledger
from kitty.errors import KittyError


class MemberRateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.s = ledger.new_state("EUR")

    def test_new_state(self):
        self.assertEqual(ledger.new_state("eur")["base"], "EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.new_state("EURO")

    def test_add_and_resolve_case_insensitive(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.resolve(self.s, "aLiCe"), "Alice")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_member(self.s, "alice")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])

    def test_add_member_rejects(self):
        for bad in ["A,B", "A=B", "", "  "]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                ledger.add_member(self.s, bad)
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "  Bob ")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Bob"])

    def test_remove_member(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        ledger.remove_member(self.s, "bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Nobody")

    def test_remove_member_refused_when_referenced(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"].append({"id": 1, "seq": 1, "payer": "Alice", "shares": [["Bob", 100]]})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"] = []
        self.s["payments"].append({"seq": 2, "from": "Alice", "to": "Bob"})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice", "Bob"])

    def test_set_rate(self):
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "usd", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["rates"], {"USD": "0.92"})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "USD"), Decimal("0.92"))
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "EUR"), 1)
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.set_rate(self.s, "eur", "1")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.rate_for(self.s, "GBP")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty import ledger
from kitty.errors import KittyError


class MemberRateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.s = ledger.new_state("EUR")

    def test_new_state(self):
        self.assertEqual(ledger.new_state("eur")["base"], "EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.new_state("EURO")

    def test_add_and_resolve_case_insensitive(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.resolve(self.s, "aLiCe"), "Alice")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_member(self.s, "alice")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])

    def test_add_member_rejects(self):
        for bad in ["A,B", "A=B", "", "  "]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                ledger.add_member(self.s, bad)
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "  Bob ")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Bob"])

    def test_remove_member(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        ledger.remove_member(self.s, "bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Nobody")

    def test_remove_member_refused_when_referenced(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"].append({"id": 1, "seq": 1, "payer": "Alice", "shares": [["Bob", 100]]})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"] = []
        self.s["payments"].append({"seq": 2, "from": "Alice", "to": "Bob"})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice", "Bob"])

    def test_set_rate(self):
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "usd", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["rates"], {"USD": "0.92"})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "USD"), Decimal("0.92"))
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "EUR"), 1)
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.set_rate(self.s, "eur", "1")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.rate_for(self.s, "GBP")


if __name__ == "__main__":

import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty import ledger
from kitty.errors import KittyError


class MemberRateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.s = ledger.new_state("EUR")

    def test_new_state(self):
        self.assertEqual(ledger.new_state("eur")["base"], "EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.new_state("EURO")

    def test_add_and_resolve_case_insensitive(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.resolve(self.s, "aLiCe"), "Alice")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_member(self.s, "alice")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])

    def test_add_member_rejects(self):
        for bad in ["A,B", "A=B", "", "  "]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                ledger.add_member(self.s, bad)
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "  Bob ")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Bob"])

    def test_remove_member(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        ledger.remove_member(self.s, "bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Nobody")

    def test_remove_member_refused_when_referenced(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"].append({"id": 1, "seq": 1, "payer": "Alice", "shares": [["Bob", 100]]})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"] = []
        self.s["payments"].append({"seq": 2, "from": "Alice", "to": "Bob"})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice", "Bob"])

    def test_set_rate(self):
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "usd", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["rates"], {"USD": "0.92"})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "USD"), Decimal("0.92"))
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "EUR"), 1)
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.set_rate(self.s, "eur", "1")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.rate_for(self.s, "GBP")


class ExpensePaymentTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.s = ledger.new_state("EUR")
        for name in ["Alice", "Bob", "Cara"]:
            ledger.add_member(self.s, name)
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "USD", "0.92")

    def shares_of(self, **kw):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", kw.pop("amount", "10"), "X", **kw)
        return self.s["expenses"][-1]["shares"]

    def test_equal_split_everyone(self):
        self.assertEqual(ledger.add_expense(self.s, "alice", "10", "Taxi"), 1)
        e = self.s["expenses"][0]
        self.assertEqual(e["shares"], [["Alice", 334], ["Bob", 333], ["Cara", 333]])
        self.assertEqual(e["payer"], "Alice")
        self.assertEqual(e["category"], "other")
        self.assertEqual(e["currency"], "EUR")
        self.assertEqual(e["date"], date.today().isoformat())

    def test_foreign_currency_locks_rate(self):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "45", "Dinner", among="Alice,Bob",
                           currency="usd", date="2026-07-14", category="food")
        e = self.s["expenses"][0]
        self.assertEqual(e["base_amount"], 4140)
        self.assertEqual(e["amount"], 4500)
        self.assertEqual(e["currency"], "USD")
        self.assertEqual(e["rate"], "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(e["shares"], [["Alice", 2070], ["Bob", 2070]])
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "USD", "0.95")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["expenses"][0]["base_amount"], 4140)

    def test_among_order(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(among="Cara,Alice"), [["Cara", 500], ["Alice", 500]])
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(among="Cara,Alice", amount="10.01"),
                         [["Cara", 501], ["Alice", 500]])

    def test_shares(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(shares="Alice=1,Bob=2"), [["Alice", 334], ["Bob", 666]])

    def test_percent(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(percent="Alice=60,Bob=40"), [["Alice", 600], ["Bob", 400]])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(percent="Alice=60,Bob=30")

    def test_exact_foreign(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(amount="45", exact="Alice=30,Bob=15", currency="USD"),
                         [["Alice", 2760], ["Bob", 1380]])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(amount="45", exact="Alice=30,Bob=14", currency="USD")

    def test_split_duplicate_case_insensitive(self):
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(among="alice,ALICE")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(shares="Bob=1,bob=1")

    def test_split_errors(self):
        bad_calls = [
            dict(among="Alice,Zed"),
            dict(among="Alice", shares="Alice=1"),
            dict(shares="Alice=0"),
            dict(shares="Alice"),
            dict(currency="GBP"),
            dict(amount="12.345"),
        ]
        for kw in bad_calls:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=kw):
                self.shares_of(**kw)
        self.assertEqual(self.s["expenses"], [])
        self.assertEqual(self.s["next_id"], 1)

    def test_no_members_is_error(self):
        s = ledger.new_state("EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "10", "X")
        ledger.add_member(s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(s, "Bob")
        ledger.remove_member(s, "Bob")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "10", "X")  # a lone member is fine

    def test_zero_base_amount_is_error(self):
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "JPY", "0.004")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(amount="1", currency="JPY")

    def test_ids_never_reused(self):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "A")
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "B")
        ledger.remove_expense(self.s, "2")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "C"), 3)
        self.assertEqual([e["id"] for e in self.s["expenses"]], [1, 3])
        for bad in ["9", "x", "2"]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                ledger.remove_expense(self.s, bad)

    def test_payment(self):
        ledger.add_payment(self.s, "bob", "Alice", "20.70")
        p = self.s["payments"][0]
        self.assertEqual((p["from"], p["to"], p["base_amount"]), ("Bob", "Alice", 2070))
        self.assertEqual(p["currency"], "EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "bob", "5")

    def test_payment_foreign_locks_rate(self):
        ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "Alice", "10", currency="usd", date="2026-07-15")
        p = self.s["payments"][0]
        self.assertEqual((p["amount"], p["base_amount"], p["rate"], p["date"]),
                         (1000, 920, "0.92", "2026-07-15"))
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "Alice", "10", currency="GBP")

    def test_expenses_and_payments_share_sequence(self):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "A")
        ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "Alice", "1")
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "B")
        self.assertEqual([e["seq"] for e in self.s["expenses"]], [1, 3])
        self.assertEqual(self.s["payments"][0]["seq"], 2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def _state(*members):
    s = ledger.new_state("EUR")
    for m in members:
        ledger.add_member(s, m)
    ledger.set_rate(s, "USD", "0.92")
    return s


class ReportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def spec_state(self):
        s = _state("Alice", "Bob")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "45", "Dinner", currency="USD",
                           date="2026-07-14", category="food")
        return s

    def test_spec_example(self):
        s = self.spec_state()
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances(s), {"Alice": 2070, "Bob": -2070})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.settle(s), [("Bob", "Alice", 2070)])
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history(s, "bob"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": -2070, "balance": -2070}])
        self.assertEqual(ledger.report(s), {"food": {"Alice": 2070, "Bob": 2070}})

    def test_payment_moves_balances(self):
        s = self.spec_state()
        ledger.add_payment(s, "Bob", "Alice", "20.70", date="2026-07-15")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances(s), {"Alice": 0, "Bob": 0})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.settle(s), [])
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history(s, "Alice")[-1], {
            "date": "2026-07-15", "description": "Payment from Bob", "change": -2070, "balance": 0})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history(s, "Bob")[-1], {
            "date": "2026-07-15", "description": "Payment to Alice", "change": 2070, "balance": 0})

    def test_payer_without_share_gets_line(self):
        s = _state("Alice", "Bob", "Cara")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Cara", "10", "Gift", among="Alice,Bob", date="2026-07-01")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history(s, "Cara"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-01", "description": "Gift", "change": 1000, "balance": 1000}])

    def test_history_sorted_by_date_then_order(self):
        s = _state("Alice", "Bob")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Bob", "10", "B", date="2026-07-02")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Bob", "10", "A", date="2026-07-01")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "10", "C", date="2026-07-02")
        h = ledger.history(s, "Alice")
        self.assertEqual([x["description"] for x in h], ["A", "B", "C"])
        self.assertEqual([x["balance"] for x in h], [-500, -1000, -500])
        self.assertEqual(h[-1]["balance"], ledger.balances(s)["Alice"])

    def test_history_unrelated_member_is_empty(self):
        s = self.spec_state()
        ledger.add_member(s, "Cara")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history(s, "cara"), [])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.history(s, "Zed")

    def test_settle_ties_alphabetical_casefold(self):
        s = _state("bob", "Alice", "Cara", "dan")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Cara", "20", "x", among="bob,Alice")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "dan", "20", "y", among="bob,Alice")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances(s), {"bob": -2000, "Alice": -2000, "Cara": 2000, "dan": 2000})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.settle(s), [("Alice", "Cara", 2000), ("bob", "dan", 2000)])

    def test_settle_partial(self):
        s = _state("Alice", "Bob", "Cara")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "30", "x")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.settle(s), [("Bob", "Alice", 1000), ("Cara", "Alice", 1000)])

    def test_settle_largest_first(self):
        s = _state("Alice", "Bob", "Cara", "Dan")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "10", "x", among="Bob")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Dan", "30", "y", among="Cara")
        # Alice +10, Bob -10, Cara -30, Dan +30
        self.assertEqual(ledger.settle(s), [("Cara", "Dan", 3000), ("Bob", "Alice", 1000)])

    def test_report_shares_not_payments(self):
        s = _state("Alice", "Bob", "Cara")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "30", "Bus", category="transport")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Cara", "10", "Lunch", among="Bob,Alice", category="food")
        ledger.add_payment(s, "Bob", "Alice", "5")
        r = ledger.report(s)
        self.assertEqual(list(r), ["food", "transport"])
        self.assertEqual(r["food"], {"Alice": 500, "Bob": 500})
        self.assertEqual(list(r["food"]), ["Alice", "Bob"])
        self.assertEqual(r["transport"], {"Alice": 1000, "Bob": 1000, "Cara": 1000})

    def test_balances_sum_zero(self):
        s = _state("Alice", "Bob", "Cara")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "45.67", "a", currency="USD")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Bob", "10", "b", shares="Alice=1,Cara=2")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Cara", "99.99", "c", percent="Alice=33.33,Bob=33.33,Cara=33.34",
                           currency="USD")
        ledger.add_payment(s, "Bob", "Alice", "3.21", currency="USD")
        self.assertEqual(sum(ledger.balances(s).values()), 0)
        total_settle = ledger.settle(s)
        self.assertTrue(all(c > 0 for _, _, c in total_settle))


if __name__ == "__main__":

import unittest
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty import ledger
from kitty.errors import KittyError


class MemberRateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.s = ledger.new_state("EUR")

    def test_new_state(self):
        self.assertEqual(ledger.new_state("eur")["base"], "EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.new_state("EURO")

    def test_add_and_resolve_case_insensitive(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.resolve(self.s, "aLiCe"), "Alice")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_member(self.s, "alice")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])

    def test_add_member_rejects(self):
        for bad in ["A,B", "A=B", "", "  "]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                ledger.add_member(self.s, bad)
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "  Bob ")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Bob"])

    def test_remove_member(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        ledger.remove_member(self.s, "bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice"])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Nobody")

    def test_remove_member_refused_when_referenced(self):
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"].append({"id": 1, "seq": 1, "payer": "Alice", "shares": [["Bob", 100]]})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.s["expenses"] = []
        self.s["payments"].append({"seq": 2, "from": "Alice", "to": "Bob"})
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.remove_member(self.s, "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["members"], ["Alice", "Bob"])

    def test_set_rate(self):
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "usd", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["rates"], {"USD": "0.92"})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "USD"), Decimal("0.92"))
        self.assertEqual(ledger.rate_for(self.s, "EUR"), 1)
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.set_rate(self.s, "eur", "1")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.rate_for(self.s, "GBP")


class ExpensePaymentTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.s = ledger.new_state("EUR")
        for name in ["Alice", "Bob", "Cara"]:
            ledger.add_member(self.s, name)
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "USD", "0.92")

    def shares_of(self, **kw):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", kw.pop("amount", "10"), "X", **kw)
        return self.s["expenses"][-1]["shares"]

    def test_equal_split_everyone(self):
        self.assertEqual(ledger.add_expense(self.s, "alice", "10", "Taxi"), 1)
        e = self.s["expenses"][0]
        self.assertEqual(e["shares"], [["Alice", 334], ["Bob", 333], ["Cara", 333]])
        self.assertEqual(e["payer"], "Alice")
        self.assertEqual(e["category"], "other")
        self.assertEqual(e["currency"], "EUR")
        self.assertEqual(e["date"], date.today().isoformat())

    def test_foreign_currency_locks_rate(self):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "45", "Dinner", among="Alice,Bob",
                           currency="usd", date="2026-07-14", category="food")
        e = self.s["expenses"][0]
        self.assertEqual(e["base_amount"], 4140)
        self.assertEqual(e["amount"], 4500)
        self.assertEqual(e["currency"], "USD")
        self.assertEqual(e["rate"], "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(e["shares"], [["Alice", 2070], ["Bob", 2070]])
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "USD", "0.95")
        self.assertEqual(self.s["expenses"][0]["base_amount"], 4140)

    def test_among_order(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(among="Cara,Alice"), [["Cara", 500], ["Alice", 500]])
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(among="Cara,Alice", amount="10.01"),
                         [["Cara", 501], ["Alice", 500]])

    def test_shares(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(shares="Alice=1,Bob=2"), [["Alice", 334], ["Bob", 666]])

    def test_percent(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(percent="Alice=60,Bob=40"), [["Alice", 600], ["Bob", 400]])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(percent="Alice=60,Bob=30")

    def test_exact_foreign(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(amount="45", exact="Alice=30,Bob=15", currency="USD"),
                         [["Alice", 2760], ["Bob", 1380]])
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(amount="45", exact="Alice=30,Bob=14", currency="USD")

    def test_split_duplicate_case_insensitive(self):
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(among="alice,ALICE")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(shares="Bob=1,bob=1")

    def test_split_errors(self):
        bad_calls = [
            dict(among="Alice,Zed"),
            dict(among="Alice", shares="Alice=1"),
            dict(shares="Alice=0"),
            dict(shares="Alice"),
            dict(currency="GBP"),
            dict(amount="12.345"),
        ]
        for kw in bad_calls:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=kw):
                self.shares_of(**kw)
        self.assertEqual(self.s["expenses"], [])
        self.assertEqual(self.s["next_id"], 1)

    def test_no_members_is_error(self):
        s = ledger.new_state("EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "10", "X")
        ledger.add_member(s, "Alice")
        ledger.add_member(s, "Bob")
        ledger.remove_member(s, "Bob")
        ledger.add_expense(s, "Alice", "10", "X")  # a lone member is fine

    def test_zero_base_amount_is_error(self):
        ledger.set_rate(self.s, "JPY", "0.004")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            self.shares_of(amount="1", currency="JPY")

    def test_ids_never_reused(self):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "A")
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "B")
        ledger.remove_expense(self.s, "2")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "C"), 3)
        self.assertEqual([e["id"] for e in self.s["expenses"]], [1, 3])
        for bad in ["9", "x", "2"]:
            with self.assertRaises(KittyError, msg=bad):
                ledger.remove_expense(self.s, bad)

    def test_payment(self):
        ledger.add_payment(self.s, "bob", "Alice", "20.70")
        p = self.s["payments"][0]
        self.assertEqual((p["from"], p["to"], p["base_amount"]), ("Bob", "Alice", 2070))
        self.assertEqual(p["currency"], "EUR")
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "bob", "5")

    def test_payment_foreign_locks_rate(self):
        ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "Alice", "10", currency="usd", date="2026-07-15")
        p = self.s["payments"][0]
        self.assertEqual((p["amount"], p["base_amount"], p["rate"], p["date"]),
                         (1000, 920, "0.92", "2026-07-15"))
        with self.assertRaises(KittyError):
            ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "Alice", "10", currency="GBP")

    def test_expenses_and_payments_share_sequence(self):
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "A")
        ledger.add_payment(self.s, "Bob", "Alice", "1")
        ledger.add_expense(self.s, "Alice", "10", "B")
        self.assertEqual([e["seq"] for e in self.s["expenses"]], [1, 3])
        self.assertEqual(self.s["payments"][0]["seq"], 2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import csv
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def run(d, *args):
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=ROOT)
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty", *args], cwd=d, env=env,
                          capture_output=True, text=True)


class CliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.d = self._tmp.name

    def tearDown(self):
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def ok(self, *args):
        r = run(self.d, *args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, f"{args}: {r.stderr}")
        self.assertEqual(r.stderr, "")
        return r.stdout

    def fails(self, *args):
        r = run(self.d, *args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 1, f"{args}: {r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
        self.assertNotEqual(r.stderr, "", args)
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", r.stderr, args)
        return r

    def setup_spec(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("init", "EUR"), "")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Alice")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Bob")
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner", "--currency", "USD",
                                 "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food"), "1\n")

    def test_spec_walkthrough(self):
        self.setup_spec()
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("member", "list"), '["Alice", "Bob"]\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "list"),
                         '[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", '
                         '"amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", '
                         '"shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]\n')

1	# kitty — shared trip expenses: design
2	
3	## Intent
4	
5	Friends on group trips currently settle up with spreadsheets and arguments at
6	the end. `kitty` replaces that with something **simple and predictable**: a
7	command-line tool that records who paid what, how each cost is split, and at
8	the end says who owes whom. Every number it prints must be reproducible by
9	hand from the rules below — no hidden rounding, no surprising re-computation.
10	
11	## Goals
12	
13	- Record members, expenses (with flexible splits and currencies) and repayments.
14	- Show balances, a deterministic settle-up plan, per-person history, a
15	  per-category spending report, and a CSV export.
16	- Scriptable: reporting commands print JSON in fixed shapes.
17	- Robust: bad input is a clean error, never a traceback, never a corrupted file.
18	
19	## Non-goals
20	
21	- Fewest-possible-payments optimisation (settle uses a specific greedy method).
22	- Live exchange rates, multiple kitties per folder, editing entries in place
23	  (remove and re-add instead), listing/removing payments (not requested; can
24	  be added later), any third-party dependency.
25	
26	## Anti-goals (would be a failure even if it "works")
27	
28	- Balances that don't sum to exactly zero, or that change on their own
29	  (e.g. because a rate was changed later).
30	- Floating-point arithmetic anywhere in money handling.
31	- An error that leaves `kitty.json` partially written or modified.
32	
33	## Constraints
34	
35	- Python standard library only. Must run on **Python 3.9** (the installed
36	  version is 3.9.6) — no `match`, no `X | Y` type syntax at runtime.
37	- Run as `python3 -m kitty <command>` from the project folder (package `kitty/`
38	  with `__main__.py`).
39	- All state in `kitty.json` in the current working directory.
40	
41	## Approaches considered
42	
43	1. **Small package with separated layers (chosen).** `money.py` (parsing,
44	   conversion, cent-splitting — pure functions on int cents / `Decimal`),
45	   `ledger.py` (members, expenses, payments, balances, settle, history,
46	   report — pure logic over loaded data), `storage.py` (read/write
47	   `kitty.json`), `cli.py` (argparse, JSON output, error → exit 1). Tests with
48	   `unittest`, both unit-level on the money rules and end-to-end through the
49	   real command in a temp directory. Chosen because the rounding rules are what
50	   the user most needs to trust, so they must be isolated and directly tested.
51	2. **Event log, recompute everything on each run.** Little benefit because
52	   rates and splits are locked at record time; adds a way for results to drift.
53	3. **Single-file script.** Faster to write, but mixes money logic with CLI
54	   parsing and fights the `python3 -m kitty` package layout.
55	
56	## Data rules (decided by the user)
57	
58	### Money and amounts
59	- All arithmetic uses `Decimal` / integer cents. Never floats.
60	- An amount argument must be a positive number with at most two decimal
61	  places. `12.345`, `0`, `-5`, `abc` are errors (no rounding of input).
62	- Output money is a string with exactly two decimals, e.g. `"41.40"`,
63	  `"-20.70"`.
64	
65	### Currencies and rates
66	- Currency codes are three letters, accepted in any case, stored uppercase.
67	- `init EUR` sets the base currency. The base currency always has rate 1.
68	- `rate set USD 0.92` means 1 USD = 0.92 base. Setting a rate for the base
69	  currency is an error. Rate must be a positive decimal.
70	- Conversion: `amount × rate`, rounded to the cent, **halves rounded up**
71	  (`ROUND_HALF_UP`).
72	- Each expense and payment **stores the rate in force when it was added** and
73	  its converted base amount. Later `rate set` never changes existing entries.
74	- Using a currency with no rate set is an error.
75	
76	### Splitting (always in base-currency cents, after conversion)
77	Let `T` be the converted base total in cents.
78	- **Equal (default: everyone)**: participants are all current members in the
79	  order they joined. Each gets `floor(T / n)`; the leftover cents go one each
80	  to participants in order. 10.00 among Alice, Bob, Cara → 3.34, 3.33, 3.33.
81	- **`--among A,B`**: same as equal, among only those listed, in the order
82	  listed.
83	- **`--shares A=2,B=1`**: weights are positive whole numbers. Each portion is
84	  `floor(T × w / Σw)`; leftover cents go one each in listed order.
85	  10.00 with `A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
86	- **`--percent A=60,B=40`**: values must total exactly 100; handled as
87	  weights exactly like shares (portion `floor(T × p / 100)`, leftovers in
88	  listed order).
89	- **`--exact A=30,B=20`**: values are in the expense's own currency and must
90	  add up exactly to the expense amount (else error); then they are treated as
91	  weights on `T` exactly like shares.
92	- Only one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares`, `--percent` per expense.
93	- Every name in a split must be a current member; no name may appear twice.
94	- Splits are computed **once, when the expense is added**, and stored. Members
95	  who join later are not part of earlier "everyone" expenses.
96	- Shares therefore always sum to exactly `T`.
97	
98	### Members
99	- Names are **case-insensitive**: "alice" and "Alice" are the same person.
100	  Adding a name that matches an existing one case-insensitively is an error.
101	  Every command accepts any spelling; output always uses the name as first
102	  added.
103	- Names may not contain `,` or `=`. (Builder's call: also reject empty /
104	  whitespace-only names.)
105	- Join order is preserved and matters (equal splits, output order).
106	- `member remove` is refused if the person appears anywhere: as payer or
107	  sharer of any expense, or sender/recipient of any payment. Removing someone
108	  with no history is fine.
109	
110	### Payments
111	- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency C] [--date D]`: FROM's balance goes
112	  up by the base amount, TO's goes down. FROM and TO the same person is an
113	  error. Both must be members.
114	
115	### Balances
116	- For each member: `Σ(base amounts they paid) − Σ(their shares) +
117	  Σ(payments sent) − Σ(payments received)`. Positive = owed money.
118	
119	### Settle (greedy, deterministic)
120	While anyone has a nonzero balance: the person who owes the most (most
121	negative) pays the person who is owed the most (most positive) the smaller of
122	the two absolute amounts, so at least one of them reaches zero. Ties on either
123	side go to the name that comes first alphabetically, ignoring case
124	(`str.casefold`). Payments are listed in the order they are worked out.
125	`settle` only suggests; it records nothing.
126	
127	### Dates and categories
128	- `--date YYYY-MM-DD`, validated as a real date; default is today.
129	- `--category`, default `"other"`.
130	
131	### IDs
132	- Expenses are numbered 1, 2, 3, … ; an ID is never reused, even after
133	  removal (store a `next_id` counter).
134	
135	## Commands and output
136	
137	Reporting commands print JSON via `json.dumps` with default separators (which
138	matches the examples below exactly), followed by a newline.
139	
140	| Command | Output |
141	|---|---|
142	| `init CUR` | nothing |
143	| `member add NAME` / `member remove NAME` | nothing |
144	| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` (join order) |
145	| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION [opts]` | the new ID alone, e.g. `1` |
146	| `expense list` | see below (ID order) |
147	| `expense remove ID` | nothing; unknown ID is an error |
148	| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency] [--date]` | nothing |
149	| `rate set CUR RATE` | nothing |
150	| `balances` | `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}` |
151	| `settle` | `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]` |
152	| `history NAME` | `[{"date": ..., "description": ..., "change": ..., "balance": ...}]` |
153	| `report` | `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}` |
154	| `export FILE` | nothing; writes CSV |
155	
156	`expense list` entry:
157	`{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner",
158	"amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category":
159	"food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}` — `amount` is in the
160	expense's own currency, everything else in base. `shares` keys are in split
161	order.
162	
163	`history NAME`: every expense where the person is payer or sharer, and every
164	payment they sent or received, sorted by date then by the order added
165	(expenses and payments share one insertion sequence). `change` is their
166	balance change from that entry; `balance` is the running total. Expense lines
167	use the expense description; payments use `"Payment to Alice"` (sender's view)
168	or `"Payment from Bob"` (recipient's view). A payer with no share still gets a
169	line. The final `balance` equals that person's `balances` value.
170	
171	`report`: for each category, each person's total **share** (not what they
172	paid) of expenses in that category. Payments are excluded.
173	
174	`export FILE`: CSV with header `id,date,payer,description,amount,currency,category,base_amount`,
175	one row per expense in ID order, money as two-decimal strings. Overwrites
176	FILE if it exists.
177	
178	## Errors
179	
180	- Any error: message to **stderr**, exit status **1**, and `kitty.json` is
181	  **left unchanged** (validate fully before writing; write atomically via a
182	  temp file + rename).
183	- Includes argparse usage errors (override its default exit status 2).
184	- Any command other than `init` when `kitty.json` doesn't exist is an error;
185	  `init` when it already exists is an error.
186	- An unreadable or malformed `kitty.json` is an error, not a traceback.
187	
188	## Storage
189	
190	`kitty.json` (builder may refine the exact schema): base currency, rates
191	(as decimal strings), members in join order, expenses and payments each with a
192	shared insertion sequence number, stored rate, original amount in cents,
193	base amount in cents, and stored shares as an ordered list of `[name, cents]`;
194	plus `next_id`. Money stored as integer cents so nothing is re-rounded on
195	reload.
196	
197	## Calls I made (user can override)
198	
199	- Mutating commands other than `expense add` print nothing on success.
200	- `report`: categories in alphabetical order; within each, only people who
201	  had a share in that category, in join order. `balances` includes every
202	  current member, in join order.
203	- Category is stored as typed (so `Food` and `food` are different categories).
204	- Rates may have any number of decimal places.
205	- `--percent` values may have up to two decimals (e.g. `33.33,33.33,33.34`)
206	  and must be positive; `--exact` values follow the amount rules (positive,
207	  ≤ 2 decimals).
208	- `DESCRIPTION` is a single argument (quote multi-word descriptions).
209	- Empty `settle` result is `[]`; a member with no entries has `history` `[]`.
210	- `--currency` omitted means the base currency.
211	- A foreign amount that converts to 0 base cents is an error.
212	- Names are matched with `str.casefold`; leading/trailing whitespace is
213	  stripped from new names.
214	- JSON output uses `ensure_ascii=False` so names like "Zoë" print readably
215	  (default separators otherwise, so the example shapes are unchanged).
216	- A description starting with `-` needs the usual `--` separator.
217	
218	## Left to the builder
219	
220	Module internals, exact JSON storage schema, error message wording, test
221	structure.

     5	from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
     6	from typing import List, Tuple

    10	_AMOUNT = re.compile(r"\d+(\.\d{1,2})?")
    11	_RATE = re.compile(r"\d+(\.\d+)?")
    12	_INT = re.compile(r"\d+")
    13	_CURRENCY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]{3}")
    14	_DATE = re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}")
    15	
    16	
    17	def _cents(text: str, what: str) -> int:
    18	    if not _AMOUNT.fullmatch(text):
    19	        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (use a positive number with at most two decimals)")
    20	    cents = int(Decimal(text) * 100)
    21	    if cents <= 0:
    22	        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (must be greater than zero)")
    23	    return cents
    24	
    25	
    26	def parse_amount(text: str) -> int:
    27	    return _cents(text, "amount")
    28	
    29	
    30	def parse_percent(text: str) -> int:
    31	    """Percent in hundredths, e.g. "33.33" -> 3333."""
    32	    return _cents(text, "percentage")
    33	
    34	
    35	def parse_share(text: str) -> int:
    36	    if not _INT.fullmatch(text) or int(text) <= 0:
    37	        raise KittyError(f"invalid share: {text!r} (use a positive whole number)")
    38	    return int(text)
    39	
    40	
    41	def parse_rate(text: str) -> Decimal:
    42	    if not _RATE.fullmatch(text) or Decimal(text) <= 0:
    43	        raise KittyError(f"invalid rate: {text!r} (use a positive number)")
    44	    return Decimal(text)
    45	
    46	
    47	def parse_currency(text: str) -> str:
    48	    if not _CURRENCY.fullmatch(text):
    49	        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency code: {text!r} (use three letters)")
    50	    return text.upper()
    51	
    52	
    53	def parse_date(text: str) -> str:
    54	    try:
    55	        if not _DATE.fullmatch(text):
    56	            raise ValueError
    57	        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)
    58	    except ValueError:
    59	        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r} (use YYYY-MM-DD)") from None
    60	    return text
    61	
    62	
    63	def convert(cents: int, rate: Decimal) -> int:
    64	    """Convert to base cents: amount x rate, rounded to the cent, halves up."""
    65	    return int((Decimal(cents) * rate).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
    66	
    67	
    68	def split_weighted(total: int, weights: List[Tuple[str, int]]) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
    69	    """Round each exact portion down, then hand out leftover cents in list order."""
    70	    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    71	    parts = [[name, total * w // weight_sum] for name, w in weights]
    72	    leftover = total - sum(c for _, c in parts)
    73	    for i in range(leftover):
    74	        parts[i][1] += 1
    75	    return [(name, cents) for name, cents in parts]
    76	
    77	
    78	def split_equal(total: int, names: List[str]) -> List[Tuple[str, int]]:
    79	    return split_weighted(total, [(name, 1) for name in names])
    80	
    81	
    82	def fmt(cents: int) -> str:
    83	    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
    84	    whole, frac = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
    85	    return f"{sign}{whole}.{frac:02d}"

    10

    12	def _path(directory: str) -> str:
    13	    return os.path.join(directory, FILENAME)
    14	
    15	
    16	def exists(directory: str = ".") -> bool:
    17	    return os.path.exists(_path(directory))
    18	
    19	
    20	def load(directory: str = ".") -> dict:
    21	    path = _path(directory)
    22	    if not os.path.exists(path):
    23	        raise KittyError(f"no {FILENAME} here; run init first")
    24	    try:
    25	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    26	            state = json.load(f)
    27	    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
    28	        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {FILENAME}: {e}") from None
    29	    if not isinstance(state, dict):
    30	        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {FILENAME}: not a kitty file")
    31	    return state
    32	
    33	
    34	def save(state: dict, directory: str = ".") -> None:
    35	    tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
    36	        "w", encoding="utf-8", dir=directory, prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".tmp", delete=False)
    37	    try:
    38	        with tmp:
    39	            json.dump(state, tmp, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    40	            tmp.write("\n")
    41	        os.chmod(tmp.name, 0o644)
    42	        os.replace(tmp.name, _path(directory))
    43	    except OSError as e:
    44	        if os.path.exists(tmp.name):
    45	            os.unlink(tmp.name)
    46	        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {FILENAME}: {e}") from None

    24	    key = name.strip().casefold()

    37	    if any(m.casefold() == name.casefold() for m in state["members"]):

    71	def _resolve_unique(state: dict, names: List[str]) -> List[str]:

    73	    for i, name in enumerate(resolved):

    79	def _parse_pairs(state: dict, text: str,

    85	        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
    86	        names.append(name)
    87	        values.append(parse_value(value.strip()))

I found no Critical issues and four Important ones. Three of the five focus points pass outright; focus point 1 fails on non-ASCII digits and focus point 2 fails on structurally invalid files.

## Strengths

- **Layering matches the spec.** `money.py` holds pure integer-cent and `Decimal` functions, `ledger.py` holds pure state logic, `storage.py` is small, and `cli.py` is a single dispatch. No floats appear anywhere in money handling.
- **Late errors cannot change the file.** All validation runs against the in-memory state, and `storage.save` (atomic temp file + `os.replace`) is called only after the command succeeds (cli.py:140-141). I checked focus point 3: `--among alice,Zed`, `--among alice,ALICE` and `--shares alice=1,bob=x` all left `kitty.json` byte-identical.
- **Duplicate names under different case are caught.** `_resolve_unique` (ledger.py:71) compares names after resolving them to their canonical spelling, so `alice,ALICE` is rejected (focus point 4 passes).
- **Split portions always sum to the total.** `split_weighted` uses exact integer floor division, and the leftover is always smaller than the number of people, so it can't overrun. A randomised test covers this (test_money.py:73). Focus point 5 passes.
- **Bad amounts are rejected.** `fullmatch` with a strict regex runs before `Decimal` ever sees the text. NaN, Infinity, 1e3, " 5", "+5", "5." and 0.00 all exit 1 cleanly.
- **Argparse errors behave.** Usage errors go through `_Parser.error`, so they exit 1, and `parser_class` is passed down to every subparser.
- Settle's tie-breaking, history ordering by (date, seq), report ordering, IDs that are never reused, and rates locked at record time all match the spec. The rulings in progress.md are reasonable.
- All 58 tests pass.

## Issues

### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

### Important (Should Fix)

**1. A `kitty.json` that parses but has the wrong structure crashes with a traceback** (storage.py:29-31; focus point 2)
- **What's wrong:** `load` only checks that the top level is a dict.
- **Reproduction:**
  - `echo '{}' > kitty.json; python3 -m kitty balances` gives `KeyError: 'members'` and a traceback.
  - `"members": 5` gives `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable`.
  - An expense of `{"id":1}` gives `KeyError: 'payer'` on `balances`. Worse, `member add Q` on that same file succeeds and rewrites it.
- **Why it matters:** the spec says "An unreadable or malformed `kitty.json` is an error, not a traceback", and a hand-edited or truncated file is exactly this case. The plan's test (`test_load_malformed`) only covers invalid JSON and non-objects, so this gap is partly the plan's fault.
- **Fix:** add a `_validate(state)` step in `load` that checks:
  - the required keys are present;
  - each field has the right type: `members` is a list of str, `expenses` and `payments` are lists of dicts with the expected keys and int cents, and `next_id` and `next_seq` are ints;
  - every name referenced in an entry is a member.
  
  Raise `KittyError` on any mismatch. A cheaper backstop is to also catch `(KeyError, TypeError, ValueError)` around the command run and report "kitty.json is malformed". That alone does not stop a mutating command from re-saving a corrupt file.

**2. A directory you can't write to gives a traceback** (storage.py:35)
- **What's wrong:** `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(...)` is called outside the `try`, so a `PermissionError` while creating the temp file isn't converted.
- **Reproduction:** run `init EUR` in a `chmod 555` directory, or `member add Al` where `kitty.json` exists but the directory is read-only. Both print `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: './.kitty-XXXX.tmp'` with a traceback.
- **Fix:** move the temp-file creation inside the `try`, or wrap it in its own `except OSError`. Guard the `unlink` in case `tmp` was never assigned.

**3. Very large amounts or rates crash, and some are silently rounded** (money.py:20, money.py:65)
- **What's wrong:** both lines compute in the default `Decimal` context, which keeps only 28 significant digits.
- **Reproduction:**
  - `expense add Alice 100000000000000000000000000 big` gives `decimal.InvalidOperation` with a traceback, because `quantize` needs more than 28 digits.
  - `rate set USD 1000000000000000000000000000000`, then `expense add Alice 1 x --currency USD`, gives the same traceback.
  - Silent rounding: `convert(1, parse_rate("0.4" + "9"*29))` returns `1`. The correct result is 0, which would be the "less than one cent" error. The product was first rounded half-even to 0.5, then rounded up again.
- **Why it matters:** nobody types 27-digit amounts on a trip, but the spec promises "never a traceback" and "every number reproducible by hand". The double rounding contradicts the `ROUND_HALF_UP` rule.
- **Fix:**
  - Parse cents without `Decimal`: split the text on `.` and compute `int(whole)*100 + int(frac.ljust(2, "0"))`.
  - In `convert`, compute exactly with integers: turn the rate into an integer fraction n/d, then use `(cents*n*2 + d) // (2*d)`. Alternatively, run the multiply inside `localcontext()` with enough precision and trap `Inexact`.
  - Optionally cap the input length.

**4. `export kitty.json` overwrites the ledger with CSV** (cli.py:79-81)
- **Reproduction:** `python3 -m kitty export kitty.json` exits 0. `kitty.json` now begins `id,date,payer,...`, and every later command fails with "cannot read kitty.json". All data is gone.
- **Why it matters:** the spec does say export "overwrites FILE if it exists". But a reasonable user would not expect one typo to wipe the trip's ledger, and it breaks the "never a corrupted file" goal.
- **Fix:** refuse when `os.path.realpath(path) == os.path.realpath("kitty.json")` (or use `os.path.samefile` when the file exists).

### Minor (Nice to Have)

**5. Non-ASCII digits are accepted as numbers** (money.py:10-13)
- **What's wrong:** Python's `\d` matches any Unicode decimal digit, and `Decimal` and `int` both accept them.
- **Reproduction:**
  - `expense add Alice ٥ x` (Arabic-Indic five) records 5.00.
  - `expense add Alice １０ x` (full-width digits) records 10.00.
  - `--shares alice=٣,bob=1` is accepted as weight 3.
  - Dates happen to be rejected, but only because `fromisoformat` refuses them.
- **Why it matters:** this is the "strings `Decimal` accepts but the spec forbids" class from focus point 1. The plan's regex `^\d+...$` carries the same flaw.
- **Fix:** use `[0-9]` or compile with `re.ASCII`.

**6. Expense IDs must match exactly** (ledger.py:153)
`expense remove 01` reports "no expense with ID 01". Parsing the ID as a non-negative int would be friendlier. Very low impact.

**7. Missing tests**
- `--among ''` and trailing commas (`alice,`) give "unknown member: " with an empty name. That's acceptable, but the message is unclear and there's no test.
- Nothing tests the read-only directory case or a `kitty.json` that is valid JSON with the wrong structure. These would have caught issues 1 and 2.

## Declined to judge

- **CSV formula injection** (descriptions starting with `=`): not in the spec, and the export is for the user's own data.
- **Saving forces mode 0644 regardless of umask:** already recorded as a ruling in the ledger.
- **`os.replace` turns a symlinked `kitty.json` into a regular file:** an unusual environment the spec doesn't mention.
- **The CSV export is not written atomically:** the atomicity rule covers `kitty.json` only, and a partial CSV loses nothing.
- **BrokenPipeError when output is piped to `head`:** general CLI polish outside the spec's error model.
- **`RecursionError` on a deeply nested `kitty.json`:** contrived input. Issue 1's fix should catch it anyway.
- **People whose share rounds to 0 cents** (e.g. 0.01 split three ways) show up in `report` as "0.00" and get a 0.00 `history` line, which also blocks their removal. This is consistent with "appears as sharer" in the spec, so I left it.
- **Empty `--category ""` and empty description are accepted:** the spec is silent and it does no harm.
- **Argparse prefix matching** (`--am` means `--among`): standard argparse behaviour, not a defect.

## Recommendations

- Add a schema validation step in `storage.load`, with tests for `{}`, a missing key, a wrong type, and an entry that names an unknown member.
- Do all of the money parsing and conversion in exact integer arithmetic. That removes the 28-digit limit and the double rounding together.
- Switch the number regexes to ASCII-only `[0-9]`. The plan's Interfaces block should say this too.
- Guard `export` against writing onto `kitty.json`.

## Assessment

**Ready to merge?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** The core money rules, splits, settle and atomic writes are correct and well tested. But the spec's explicit "never a traceback" promise is broken by realistic inputs: a `kitty.json` with the wrong structure and a directory you can't write to. `export kitty.json` can also destroy the ledger. All of these are small, contained fixes.

The probe script I used is at `/private/tmp/tmp6o6qezvs/tmp/kittyprobe/probe.sh`. I left the worktree untouched.

You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture, design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

## What Was Implemented

`kitty`, a stdlib-only Python 3.9 CLI (`python3 -m kitty <command>`) for shared trip expenses stored in `kitty.json` in the current directory: members, expenses with equal/among/exact/shares/percent splits, foreign currencies with rates locked at record time, payments, balances, greedy settle, history, category report, CSV export. Package `kitty/` (money.py, ledger.py, storage.py, cli.py, errors.py, __main__.py) with unittest tests in `tests/`.

## Requirements / Plan

- Spec (binding authority): docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-kitty-design.md

I found no Critical issues and four Important ones. Three of the five focus points pass outright; focus point 1 fails on non-ASCII digits and focus point 2 fails on structurally invalid files.

## Strengths

- **Layering matches the spec.** `money.py` holds pure integer-cent and `Decimal` functions, `ledger.py` holds pure state logic, `storage.py` is small, and `cli.py` is a single dispatch. No floats appear anywhere in money handling.
- **Late errors cannot change the file.** All validation runs against the in-memory state, and `storage.save` (atomic temp file + `os.replace`) is called only after the command succeeds (cli.py:140-141). I checked focus point 3: `--among alice,Zed`, `--among alice,ALICE` and `--shares alice=1,bob=x` all left `kitty.json` byte-identical.
- **Duplicate names under different case are caught.** `_resolve_unique` (ledger.py:71) compares names after resolving them to their canonical spelling, so `alice,ALICE` is rejected (focus point 4 passes).
- **Split portions always sum to the total.** `split_weighted` uses exact integer floor division, and the leftover is always smaller than the number of people, so it can't overrun. A randomised test covers this (test_money.py:73). Focus point 5 passes.
- **Bad amounts are rejected.** `fullmatch` with a strict regex runs before `Decimal` ever sees the text. NaN, Infinity, 1e3, " 5", "+5", "5." and 0.00 all exit 1 cleanly.
- **Argparse errors behave.** Usage errors go through `_Parser.error`, so they exit 1, and `parser_class` is passed down to every subparser.
- Settle's tie-breaking, history ordering by (date, seq), report ordering, IDs that are never reused, and rates locked at record time all match the spec. The rulings in progress.md are reasonable.
- All 58 tests pass.

## Issues

### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

### Important (Should Fix)

**1. A `kitty.json` that parses but has the wrong structure crashes with a traceback** (storage.py:29-31; focus point 2)
- **What's wrong:** `load` only checks that the top level is a dict.
- **Reproduction:**
  - `echo '{}' > kitty.json; python3 -m kitty balances` gives `KeyError: 'members'` and a traceback.
  - `"members": 5` gives `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable`.
  - An expense of `{"id":1}` gives `KeyError: 'payer'` on `balances`. Worse, `member add Q` on that same file succeeds and rewrites it.
- **Why it matters:** the spec says "An unreadable or malformed `kitty.json` is an error, not a traceback", and a hand-edited or truncated file is exactly this case. The plan's test (`test_load_malformed`) only covers invalid JSON and non-objects, so this gap is partly the plan's fault.
- **Fix:** add a `_validate(state)` step in `load` that checks:
  - the required keys are present;
  - each field has the right type: `members` is a list of str, `expenses` and `payments` are lists of dicts with the expected keys and int cents, and `next_id` and `next_seq` are ints;
  - every name referenced in an entry is a member.
  
  Raise `KittyError` on any mismatch. A cheaper backstop is to also catch `(KeyError, TypeError, ValueError)` around the command run and report "kitty.json is malformed". That alone does not stop a mutating command from re-saving a corrupt file.

**2. A directory you can't write to gives a traceback** (storage.py:35)
- **What's wrong:** `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(...)` is called outside the `try`, so a `PermissionError` while creating the temp file isn't converted.
- **Reproduction:** run `init EUR` in a `chmod 555` directory, or `member add Al` where `kitty.json` exists but the directory is read-only. Both print `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: './.kitty-XXXX.tmp'` with a traceback.
- **Fix:** move the temp-file creation inside the `try`, or wrap it in its own `except OSError`. Guard the `unlink` in case `tmp` was never assigned.

**3. Very large amounts or rates crash, and some are silently rounded** (money.py:20, money.py:65)
- **What's wrong:** both lines compute in the default `Decimal` context, which keeps only 28 significant digits.
- **Reproduction:**
  - `expense add Alice 100000000000000000000000000 big` gives `decimal.InvalidOperation` with a traceback, because `quantize` needs more than 28 digits.
  - `rate set USD 1000000000000000000000000000000`, then `expense add Alice 1 x --currency USD`, gives the same traceback.
  - Silent rounding: `convert(1, parse_rate("0.4" + "9"*29))` returns `1`. The correct result is 0, which would be the "less than one cent" error. The product was first rounded half-even to 0.5, then rounded up again.
- **Why it matters:** nobody types 27-digit amounts on a trip, but the spec promises "never a traceback" and "every number reproducible by hand". The double rounding contradicts the `ROUND_HALF_UP` rule.
- **Fix:**
  - Parse cents without `Decimal`: split the text on `.` and compute `int(whole)*100 + int(frac.ljust(2, "0"))`.
  - In `convert`, compute exactly with integers: turn the rate into an integer fraction n/d, then use `(cents*n*2 + d) // (2*d)`. Alternatively, run the multiply inside `localcontext()` with enough precision and trap `Inexact`.
  - Optionally cap the input length.

**4. `export kitty.json` overwrites the ledger with CSV** (cli.py:79-81)
- **Reproduction:** `python3 -m kitty export kitty.json` exits 0. `kitty.json` now begins `id,date,payer,...`, and every later command fails with "cannot read kitty.json". All data is gone.
- **Why it matters:** the spec does say export "overwrites FILE if it exists". But a reasonable user would not expect one typo to wipe the trip's ledger, and it breaks the "never a corrupted file" goal.
- **Fix:** refuse when `os.path.realpath(path) == os.path.realpath("kitty.json")` (or use `os.path.samefile` when the file exists).

### Minor (Nice to Have)

**5. Non-ASCII digits are accepted as numbers** (money.py:10-13)
- **What's wrong:** Python's `\d` matches any Unicode decimal digit, and `Decimal` and `int` both accept them.
- **Reproduction:**
  - `expense add Alice ٥ x` (Arabic-Indic five) records 5.00.
  - `expense add Alice １０ x` (full-width digits) records 10.00.
  - `--shares alice=٣,bob=1` is accepted as weight 3.
  - Dates happen to be rejected, but only because `fromisoformat` refuses them.
- **Why it matters:** this is the "strings `Decimal` accepts but the spec forbids" class from focus point 1. The plan's regex `^\d+...$` carries the same flaw.
- **Fix:** use `[0-9]` or compile with `re.ASCII`.

**6. Expense IDs must match exactly** (ledger.py:153)
`expense remove 01` reports "no expense with ID 01". Parsing the ID as a non-negative int would be friendlier. Very low impact.

**7. Missing tests**
- `--among ''` and trailing commas (`alice,`) give "unknown member: " with an empty name. That's acceptable, but the message is unclear and there's no test.
- Nothing tests the read-only directory case or a `kitty.json` that is valid JSON with the wrong structure. These would have caught issues 1 and 2.

## Declined to judge

- **CSV formula injection** (descriptions starting with `=`): not in the spec, and the export is for the user's own data.
- **Saving forces mode 0644 regardless of umask:** already recorded as a ruling in the ledger.
- **`os.replace` turns a symlinked `kitty.json` into a regular file:** an unusual environment the spec doesn't mention.
- **The CSV export is not written atomically:** the atomicity rule covers `kitty.json` only, and a partial CSV loses nothing.
- **BrokenPipeError when output is piped to `head`:** general CLI polish outside the spec's error model.
- **`RecursionError` on a deeply nested `kitty.json`:** contrived input. Issue 1's fix should catch it anyway.
- **People whose share rounds to 0 cents** (e.g. 0.01 split three ways) show up in `report` as "0.00" and get a 0.00 `history` line, which also blocks their removal. This is consistent with "appears as sharer" in the spec, so I left it.
- **Empty `--category ""` and empty description are accepted:** the spec is silent and it does no harm.
- **Argparse prefix matching** (`--am` means `--among`): standard argparse behaviour, not a defect.

## Recommendations

- Add a schema validation step in `storage.load`, with tests for `{}`, a missing key, a wrong type, and an entry that names an unknown member.
- Do all of the money parsing and conversion in exact integer arithmetic. That removes the 28-digit limit and the double rounding together.
- Switch the number regexes to ASCII-only `[0-9]`. The plan's Interfaces block should say this too.
- Guard `export` against writing onto `kitty.json`.

## Assessment

**Ready to merge?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** The core money rules, splits, settle and atomic writes are correct and well tested. But the spec's explicit "never a traceback" promise is broken by realistic inputs: a `kitty.json` with the wrong structure and a directory you can't write to. `export kitty.json` can also destroy the ledger. All of these are small, contained fixes.

The probe script I used is at `/private/tmp/tmp6o6qezvs/tmp/kittyprobe/probe.sh`. I left the worktree untouched.

import csv
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def run(d, *args):
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=ROOT)
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty", *args], cwd=d, env=env,
                          capture_output=True, text=True)


class CliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.d = self._tmp.name

    def tearDown(self):
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def ok(self, *args):
        r = run(self.d, *args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, f"{args}: {r.stderr}")
        self.assertEqual(r.stderr, "")
        return r.stdout

    def fails(self, *args):
        r = run(self.d, *args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 1, f"{args}: {r.stdout}{r.stderr}")
        self.assertNotEqual(r.stderr, "", args)
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", r.stderr, args)
        return r

    def setup_spec(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("init", "EUR"), "")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Alice")
        self.ok("member", "add", "Bob")
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner", "--currency", "USD",
                                 "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food"), "1\n")

"""Command-line interface: argument parsing, JSON output, errors as exit status 1."""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

from kitty import ledger, storage
from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.money import fmt


class _Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        raise KittyError(f"{message}\n{self.format_usage().rstrip()}")


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = _Parser(prog="python3 -m kitty", description="Track shared expenses on group trips.")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND", parser_class=_Parser)
    sub.required = True

    init = sub.add_parser("init", help="start a new kitty")
    init.add_argument("currency")

    member = sub.add_parser("member", help="manage members")
    msub = member.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    msub.required = True
    msub.add_parser("add").add_argument("name")
    msub.add_parser("remove").add_argument("name")
    msub.add_parser("list")

    expense = sub.add_parser("expense", help="manage expenses")
    esub = expense.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    esub.required = True
    add = esub.add_parser("add")
    add.add_argument("payer")
    add.add_argument("amount")
    add.add_argument("description")
    for opt in ["among", "exact", "shares", "percent", "currency", "date", "category"]:
        add.add_argument(f"--{opt}")
    esub.add_parser("list")
    esub.add_parser("remove").add_argument("id")

    payment = sub.add_parser("payment", help="record a repayment")
    psub = payment.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    psub.required = True
    padd = psub.add_parser("add")
    padd.add_argument("frm", metavar="from")
    padd.add_argument("to")
    padd.add_argument("amount")
    padd.add_argument("--currency")
    padd.add_argument("--date")

    rate = sub.add_parser("rate", help="set exchange rates")
    rsub = rate.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    rsub.required = True
    rset = rsub.add_parser("set")
    rset.add_argument("currency")
    rset.add_argument("rate")

    sub.add_parser("balances", help="show each person's balance")
    sub.add_parser("settle", help="suggest payments to square up")
